reading.summary: Sentences 2 and 3 give checkable support, but sentences 4 and 5 only assert, so add a real number linking sleep to learning.

sentences.text: Schools should start later in the morning.
During puberty, teenagers' body clocks shift later, so many cannot fall asleep before 11 pm.
When Seattle moved its high-school start from 7:50 to 8:45 in 2016, students slept about 34 minutes more each night.
Also it is just better and everyone knows it.
That is why a later start would help students learn.

verdicts.note: This is your claim, so it needs no proof itself, but the rest must back it up.
You name a mechanism, body clocks shifting in puberty, and a 11 pm figure a reader could look up.
Strong: a named place, year, start times and 34 minutes make this easy to check.
This only asserts; 'everyone knows it' and 'better' give nothing a reader can check.

fix.pattern: Also, [a specific measured benefit] in [place or study].

verdicts.note: This links sleep to learning, but gives no grades, test scores or attendance to show learning improved.

fix.pattern: After the change, [grades, attendance or test result] [rose or fell] by [amount].
